independent_argument: Base case retains the first item. At n≥2 each old item has probability 1/(n−1) and survives independently of its identity with probability (n−1)/n. Its final probability and that of the newcomer are both 1/n. This proves the single-item case; it does not infer general subset uniformity from marginals.

checks.illustrated_replacements: A retained initially; B replaces A; C does not replace B, one possible run
checks.memory: one item plus count; diagram may display possible outcomes

limitations: Exact finite checks supplement the stated argument; not a claim about audience understanding.
